methods.title: AMD block: average smoothing scales
methods.summary: Several fixed moving-average windows are evaluated on the prefix, then averaged with equal weights. The next step uses phase-wise means of the detrended prefix. methods.title: CEEMDAN: ensemble averaging with adaptive noise
methods.summary: CEEMDAN repeatedly estimates components from perturbed signals and updates a shared residual. The noise modes and ensemble averages are algorithmic inputs, not decorative uncertainty bands.

steps.title: Generate perturbations
steps.text: Normalize the input, draw seeded noise, and decompose the noise realizations.

steps.title: Average first IMFs
steps.text: Apply EMD to each perturbed input and average its first IMF.

steps.title: Update adaptively
steps.text: Perturb the current residual with the next noise mode, average local means, and extract the next cIMF.

steps.title: Retain the residue
steps.text: Continue until the stopping criterion, then retain the remaining signal for additive reconstruction.

parameters.name: trials
parameters.effect: Number of ensemble members; this small animation uses 8, while DeTime's default is 100.

parameters.name: epsilon
parameters.effect: Controls the perturbation scale; this visibility-oriented trace uses 0.04, not the default 0.005.

parameters.name: seed and n_jobs
parameters.effect: The trace uses seed 42 and serial execution. Preserve both for reproducibility.

parameters.name: primary_period
parameters.effect: Affects DeTime's grouping after the upstream component extraction.

cautions: Different CEEMDAN variants exist; PyEMD includes the later improved formulation documented by its authors.
An ensemble average does not establish that an IMF is a unique physical component.
Raw DeTime IMF arrays use (mode, time, channel), including a singleton channel for one series.

methods.title: EMD: estimate envelopes, subtract their mean, and sift
methods.summary: EMD adapts its oscillatory modes to the extrema of the current signal. DeTime then groups upstream modes into its trend/season/residual result.

steps.title: Locate extrema
steps.text: Local maxima and minima anchor the envelope construction.

steps.title: Build envelopes
steps.text: PyEMD interpolates upper and lower envelopes with its boundary treatment.

steps.title: Sift
steps.text: Subtract their pointwise mean, recompute extrema, and apply the stopping criteria.

steps.title: Remove the IMF
steps.text: Subtract the accepted mode from the signal and continue on the remainder.

methods.title: FreqMoE block: average frequency fits
methods.summary: This standalone operator obtains candidate periods from an FFT magnitude ranking and fits a separate harmonic projection for each one. The selected seasonal estimate is their equal-weight average. The frames expose the selection signal, rounded periods, candidate curves and averaging operation. The parameter expert_width determines the harmonic count by rounding expert_width / 64. It does not size a fitted mixture-of-experts network here.

steps.title: Separate trend and selection input
steps.text: Compute the moving-average trend. FreqMoE selects frequencies from the detrended signal; Times2D selects them from the original signal after mean removal.

steps.title: Select discrete spectral peaks
steps.text: Rank FFT magnitudes, convert bin positions into rounded integer periods, and retain distinct periods as implemented.

steps.title: Fit and average candidate seasons
steps.text: Fit a harmonic projection of the detrended signal for each selected period, then take the arithmetic mean of these projections.

steps.title: Inspect actual output streams
steps.text: The final trend, averaged projection and derived residual are checked against the public registered operator.

parameters.name: trend_window
parameters.effect: Sets the centered moving-average trend.

parameters.name: num_bands
parameters.effect: Controls how many distinct rounded FFT periods are retained.

parameters.name: expert_width
parameters.effect: Sets harmonic capacity through round(expert_width / 64).

parameters.name: fit_scope
parameters.effect: Explicitly full in this animation; prefix settings restrict the fitting interval.

cautions: The parameter expert_width determines the harmonic count by rounding expert_width / 64. It does not size a fitted mixture-of-experts network here.
A large FFT bin need not correspond to a stable physical oscillation. Trends, finite windows and rounding affect the selected periods.
The independent candidate projections are averaged, rather than jointly fitted as one combined design.
All coefficients use the selected fitting interval; no held-out forecast accuracy is shown.

methods.title: Gabor clustering: assign time-frequency atoms and reconstruct masks
methods.summary: DeTime's experimental operator builds windowed Fourier atoms, assigns their features to a supplied codebook, and reconstructs cluster-specific contributions with overlap-add.

steps.title: Window and transform
steps.text: Slide the normalized Gaussian window and compute real FFT coefficients.

steps.title: Build atom features
steps.text: Represent each time-frequency bin by normalized time, normalized frequency, and log amplitude.

steps.title: Assign the codebook
steps.text: Standardize features with the stored mean/scale and select the nearest supplied centroid.

steps.title: Mask and reconstruct
steps.text: Retain each cluster's complex coefficients, apply inverse FFT and normalized overlap-add, then group contributions heuristically.

parameters.name: model / model_path
parameters.effect: A supplied GaborClusterModel is required; the decomposition function does not train a codebook.

parameters.name: win_len / hop / n_fft
parameters.effect: Stored in the model; the example uses 48/12/64 and a Gaussian window.

parameters.name: max_clusters
parameters.effect: Optionally retains the highest-energy clusters before reconstruction.

parameters.name: trend_freq_thr
parameters.effect: Heuristic threshold on the de-standardized centroid frequency, normalized from zero to Nyquist.

cautions: This is an experimental, repository-specific operator, not a claimed reproduction of a canonical forecasting or decomposition architecture.
The fixed four-centroid teaching codebook is neither trained nor evidence of a useful scientific clustering.
The current frame grid can leave an uncovered tail when the record length is not aligned with the hop; the residual retains that difference.
Cluster labels are codebook labels; assigning low-frequency clusters to trend is a heuristic.

methods.title: LEDDAM block: fixed Gaussian smoothing
methods.summary: This standalone implementation evaluates a fixed Gaussian-weighted convolution. Its kernel is normalized to sum to one, the edge samples are replicated, and the filtered signal becomes the trend stream. Subtracting that stream from the input creates the second stream. The animation displays actual weights and local products before assembling the output. The kernel is not trained in this operator.

methods.title: Smooth, fold, and average
methods.summary: A centered uniform moving average supplies the trend; equal-phase means of the detrended series supply one repeated seasonal template.

steps.title: Slide a uniform window
steps.text: Use uniform weights over an odd-length window. DeTime increments an even requested window by one. Its NumPy mode='same' convolution uses zero extension at both ends, so the divisor remains the full window length even near an edge.

steps.title: Subtract the smooth trend
steps.text: Compute detrended = observed - trend. Folding this array into cycle rows shows the values that share each seasonal phase.

steps.title: Average seasonal phases
steps.text: For each phase offset, average the detrended values separated by season_period samples. Repeat those means along the record. If season_period is omitted, the seasonal component is identically zero.

steps.title: Center and form residual
steps.text: Subtract the mean of the complete repeated seasonal array, then return residual = observed - trend - season. This guarantees an additive identity without establishing that each assigned component is physically correct.

parameters.name: trend_window
parameters.effect: Smoothing width; even requests are advanced to the next odd integer. The animation uses 25.

parameters.name: season_period
parameters.effect: Spacing between observations assigned to the same seasonal phase; omitted means no seasonal estimate.

cautions: This is an in-package baseline, not a reproduction of a separately published forecasting model.
Zero extension pulls endpoint moving averages toward zero. Inspect boundary behavior before using the resulting components.
One repeated phase template cannot express arbitrary cycle-to-cycle shape changes.
Centered smoothing and full-record phase averaging use future observations relative to earlier time points; causal forecasting requires an origin-specific pipeline.
methods.trace_note: Window values, zero extension, uniform weights, phase averages, and centering follow the Python source. Final arrays are checked against the public Python execution path.

methods.title: MEMD: project multichannel data to estimate a joint envelope mean
methods.summary: MEMD uses many projection directions to construct a multivariate local mean. Its sifting preserves aligned mode slices across the input channels.

steps.title: Project the data
steps.text: Use Hammersley-based unit directions and locate extrema of each scalar projection.

steps.title: Construct vector envelopes
steps.text: At the projection extrema times, interpolate the original vector samples and average valid envelopes.

steps.title: Sift jointly
steps.text: Subtract the direction-averaged vector mean and repeat the multivariate stopping test.

steps.title: Extract aligned modes
steps.text: Remove the accepted multichannel IMF, continue on the vector residue, and keep the final residue.

methods.title: Extract shared modes across channels
methods.summary: A joint trajectory-matrix SVD produces modes that are reconstructed separately for each channel.

steps.title: Stack aligned windows
steps.text: Use a common window length and start positions for all channels, then stack their trajectory matrices vertically. Columns describe simultaneous multichannel windows.

steps.title: Compute shared singular modes
steps.text: Compute the exact NumPy SVD and retain the requested rank. Every matrix mode spans all channel blocks, so a mode can express related temporal structure across channels.

steps.title: Reconstruct each channel
steps.text: Split each rank-one matrix into its original channel blocks. Within each block, average entries representing the same time index to obtain one reconstructed series per channel.

steps.title: Group trend and season
steps.text: This example uses DeTime's primary-period frequency heuristic. Low-frequency modes are assigned to trend and modes near 1/period to season, with documented fallbacks if a group is empty. Residual is the observed input minus those two groups. For MSSA, the grouping frequency comes from the mean across channels of each reconstructed mode.

parameters.name: window
parameters.effect: Embedding length L; changes the temporal scale and matrix dimensions.

parameters.name: rank
parameters.effect: Number of singular modes available for grouping; more modes can retain both signal structure and noise.

parameters.name: primary_period
parameters.effect: Target period for the frequency-based seasonal grouping heuristic.

parameters.name: trend_components / season_components
parameters.effect: Optional zero-based mode indices that explicitly define the groups.

parameters.name: season_freq_tol_ratio / trend_freq_threshold
parameters.effect: Control the frequency bands used by automatic grouping.

cautions: The labels trend and season come from a grouping rule; singular-value order alone does not establish physical meaning.
Changing window, rank, or grouping can change components even when additive reconstruction remains exact.
The animation uses backend='python', speed_mode='exact'. Native or randomized fast paths are separate numerical execution choices.
This is an offline decomposition. Forecasting features must be recomputed using only observations available at each forecast origin.
Channel magnitudes affect the stacked SVD. Scale channels deliberately when units or amplitudes differ.
The current automatic grouping uses the mean across channels; opposing phases can cancel in that mean.

references.title: Golyandina and Zhigljavsky (2020), Singular Spectrum Analysis for Time Series

methods.title: Alternate between seasonal periods
methods.summary: MSTL repeatedly estimates one seasonal period while removing the current estimates of the others, then returns a trend and remainder.

steps.title: Specify the seasonal periods
steps.text: Supply the periods and their seasonal smoothing windows. This synthetic signal contains periods 12 and 36, and both are specified explicitly. The FFT panel describes the input; it is not an automatic period-selection stage in the wrapper.

steps.title: Estimate seasonal terms
steps.text: Initialize seasonal arrays at zero. For each period in the upstream processing order, fit STL to the currently adjusted series and subtract the estimated seasonal term before processing the next period.

steps.title: Add back and refine each term
steps.text: On each later pass, add back the previous estimate for the period being updated, refit that seasonal term, and subtract its replacement. This preserves the other current seasonal estimates while refining one term at a time.

steps.title: Aggregate the common output
steps.text: Use the trend from the last STL fit and subtract it from the deseasonalized series to obtain residual. DeTime sums separate upstream seasonal columns into result.season. This animation uses lmbda=None; transformed fits require the wrapper's documented original-scale allocation.

parameters.name: periods
parameters.effect: One or more integer cycle lengths. Upstream MSTL sorts them and filters periods that are too long for the record.

parameters.name: windows
parameters.effect: Odd seasonal-smoothing spans paired with the periods; this example uses 11 and 15.

parameters.name: iterate
parameters.effect: Number of passes over the seasonal terms; this example uses two.

parameters.name: lmbda
parameters.effect: Optional Box-Cox transform. None keeps the additive trace in the original scale; transformed components cannot be inverted independently and then simply added.

parameters.name: stl_kwargs
parameters.effect: Options forwarded to each STL fit, including its robustness setting.

cautions: Choose periods with enough observed repetitions. The example is illustrative and does not identify periods from data.
Closely related periods and smoothing choices can change how variation is allocated between seasonal terms.

methods.title: Reweight observations and refit
methods.summary: Residual-based robustness weights limit how strongly unusual observations influence subsequent STL smooths.

steps.title: Fit initial smooths
steps.text: DeTime's ROBUST_STL selects statsmodels STL with robust=True by default. The initial inner loop estimates seasonal and trend structure before robustness weights are updated.

steps.title: Compute robustness weights
steps.text: The first outer update uses absolute residuals from the initial fit. With h equal to six times their median, the bisquare rule assigns (1 - (abs(residual)/h)^2)^2 below h and zero above h. This example computes those weights and checks them against statsmodels.

steps.title: Refit and update the weights
steps.text: Repeated outer iterations recalculate robustness weights and refit seasonal and trend smooths. Each shown checkpoint is a fresh deterministic statsmodels fit with the indicated iteration budget; it reaches the same state for that budget.

steps.title: Retain a residual
steps.text: The wrapper returns the final trend, seasonal component, and residual. Downweighted observations remain in the input, so their unexplained values appear in the residual. The animation also displays upstream weights, which the current DeTime wrapper does not export as a result component.

parameters.name: seasonal

parameters.effect: Odd smoothing spans controlling trend and low-pass behavior; this example uses 23 and 13.

parameters.name: robust
parameters.effect: Controls the outer reweighting loop. ROBUST_STL defaults to True; setting it False disables robustness.

cautions: ROBUST_STL is the registry name for statsmodels STL with its robust option. This name does not establish implementation of other published algorithms also called RobustSTL.

methods.title: Turn overlapping windows into modes
methods.summary: SSA decomposes a lag matrix and maps its grouped modes back to time-domain components.

steps.title: Embed overlapping windows
steps.text: Slide an L-sample window across the series. Put each window in a column. Repeated observations lie on anti-diagonals, which is the Hankel structure used by SSA.

steps.title: Factor the trajectory matrix
steps.text: Compute X = U diag(s) V^T. Each singular triplet gives one rank-one matrix. Retaining only a chosen number of modes determines which matrix structure can enter subsequent grouping.

steps.title: Average each anti-diagonal
steps.text: A rank-one matrix need not itself be Hankel. Average its anti-diagonals to turn its repeated time-index estimates back into one time-domain reconstructed component.

steps.title: Group trend and season
steps.text: This example uses DeTime's primary-period frequency heuristic. Low-frequency modes are assigned to trend and modes near 1/period to season, with documented fallbacks if a group is empty. Residual is the observed input minus those two groups. Explicit component-index lists can replace this automatic grouping.

parameters.name: window
parameters.effect: Embedding length L; changes the temporal scale and matrix dimensions.

parameters.name: rank
parameters.effect: Number of singular modes available for grouping; more modes can retain both signal structure and noise.

parameters.name: primary_period
parameters.effect: Target period for the frequency-based seasonal grouping heuristic.

parameters.name: trend_components / season_components
parameters.effect: Optional zero-based mode indices that explicitly define the groups.

parameters.name: season_freq_tol_ratio / trend_freq_threshold
parameters.effect: Control the frequency bands used by automatic grouping.

cautions: The labels trend and season come from a grouping rule; singular-value order alone does not establish physical meaning.
Changing window, rank, or grouping can change components even when additive reconstruction remains exact.
The animation uses backend='python', speed_mode='exact'. Native or randomized fast paths are separate numerical execution choices.
This is an offline decomposition. Forecasting features must be recomputed using only observations available at each forecast origin.

methods.title: Separate cycle level, scale, and shape
methods.summary: STD represents each cycle using its mean, an L2 dispersion, and its own normalized shape.

steps.title: Partition and center cycles
steps.text: Split at the configured period, compute each block's arithmetic mean, and subtract it. DeTime assigns that mean to every sample of the block, producing a piecewise-constant trend. A final partial block uses the samples that exist.

steps.title: Separate dispersion and shape
steps.text: Compute the Euclidean norm of each centered block as its dispersion. Divide by that norm to obtain a unit-length seasonal shape. A block whose norm is below eps receives zero dispersion and a zero shape.

steps.title: Restore each cycle's shape
steps.text: Multiply every cycle's own normalized shape by its own dispersion. This recovers the centered block, including irregular fluctuations. Add the block mean to reconstruct the observed values.

steps.title: Compute the common result
steps.text: Return trend, the scaled seasonal term, and residual = observed - trend - season, plus dispersion and seasonal-shape arrays. Residual is approximately zero by construction for nondegenerate blocks; this behavior is part of the representation and is not a denoising result.

parameters.name: period
parameters.effect: Block length and seasonal phase convention; a wrong period changes levels, scales, and shape alignment.

parameters.name: eps
parameters.effect: Threshold below which a centered block is treated as having zero dispersion.

parameters.name: max_period_search
parameters.effect: Upper bound on the FFT-based period heuristic used only when period is omitted; this animation supplies the period explicitly.

cautions: DeTime's STD/STDR use block means and L2 norms. Dispersion is not the sample standard deviation.
STDR uses ordinary phase-wise means of normalized shapes. No robust loss, trimming, or outlier weights are used in this implementation.
A partial cycle has its own mean and norm and contributes only available phases; its scale is not directly comparable to a full cycle without accounting for length.
STD retains within-cycle irregular variation in its shape. STDR assigns deviations from a shared shape to the remainder.
The supplied period and the starting phase define block boundaries; shifting the start changes the decomposition.

references.title: Dudek (2022), STD: A Seasonal-Trend-Dispersion Decomposition of Time Series

methods.title: Average normalized cycle shapes
methods.summary: STDR uses a phase-wise average of normalized cycle shapes, then restores each cycle's dispersion and keeps a remainder.

steps.title: Form the additive result
steps.text: The final five-iteration checkpoint matches the configured DeTime STL wrapper. Residual is the input minus the returned trend and seasonal component. Reconstruction consistency does not validate a unique physical interpretation.

methods.title: ST-MTM block: smooth a phase template
methods.summary: A centered moving average estimates the prefix trend and the final trend level is held constant afterward. The next step uses phase-wise means of the detrended prefix. steps.text: Subtract the trend on the fitting prefix. Group samples by index modulo the specified period and average each phase bucket.

steps.title: Smooth the repeated template
steps.text: Tile the fitted phase means over the record. The ST-MTM variant additionally smooths that repeated curve with a centered mean.

steps.title: Inspect the derived residual
steps.text: Compute input minus the implemented trend and seasonal estimate. This residual is part of a retrospective decomposition, not a forecast score.

methods.summary: VMD alternates between frequency-domain mode updates and spectral-energy centers. DeTime's grouping into trend and season is a separate step after this optimization.

steps.text: Mirror the signal, compute its FFT, and retain the positive-frequency representation.

steps.text: Fit the remaining spectrum with a bandwidth penalty around the current center frequency.

steps.text: Use the mode's positive-frequency energy to update its center, then repeat across modes.

steps.title: Reconstruct and group
steps.text: Complete the conjugate spectrum, invert the FFT, crop the mirrored margins, and group modes.

methods.title: WaveletMixer block: combine detail bands
methods.summary: The implemented operator delegates the transform to PyWavelets. It reconstructs the coarsest approximation as trend and selected detail arrays as season, then derives the residual by subtraction. The animation exposes the analysis filter taps, coefficient arrays and inverse reconstructions. The WaveForM and WaveletMixer identifiers have different default wavelets and selected bands; neither operator runs the cited complete forecasting backbone.

steps.title: Analyze with fixed wavelet filters
steps.text: PyWavelets applies the selected analysis filters to produce approximation and detail coefficients at several resolutions.

steps.title: Reconstruct the approximation
steps.text: Keep only the coarsest approximation coefficients, zero the other coefficient arrays and apply inverse reconstruction to obtain the trend.

steps.title: Reconstruct selected detail bands
steps.text: Keep the explicitly selected coefficient-list positions and reconstruct their combined sample-aligned contribution as season.

steps.title: Inspect the remaining detail
steps.text: The residual is the observed input minus the approximation and selected details. All displayed components match the public operator.

parameters.name: wavelet
parameters.effect: Selects the fixed analysis/synthesis wavelet family; db4 and sym4 are used by these two examples.

parameters.name: level
parameters.effect: Requests decomposition depth, limited by the implementation using the input length and filter length.

parameters.name: season_levels
parameters.effect: Contains coefficient-list positions: 1 denotes cD_L, 2 denotes cD_(L-1), and so on; position 0 is the trend approximation.

cautions: WaveForM's graph enhancement and WaveletMixer's trained mixing layers are outside these standalone operators.
The source uses PyWavelets' default symmetric boundary extension; boundary values depend on that convention.
A selected frequency-scale band is called season by the common result contract; periodic interpretation requires separate evidence.
The coefficient heatmap pads unequal-length arrays with zeros for display only. Computation uses their original lengths.

methods.title: xPatch block: exponential level updates
methods.summary: The implemented xPatch-inspired block offers EMA and a Holt-style level/slope option named dema. This animation uses EMA with alpha = 0.25, followed by the optional five-sample smoother of the nontrend stream. It shows the exact two-term update and the effect of a second alpha. The raw EMA is one-sided; the selected centered seasonal smoother changes that information boundary.

steps.title: Mix observation and state
steps.text: Initialize the level with the first sample, then update it as alpha times the observation plus one minus alpha times the previous level.

steps.title: Advance the recurrence
steps.text: Continue the EMA update through the record. A second, explicitly labelled alpha illustrates a parameter change.

steps.title: Smooth the difference
steps.text: This example smooths input minus trend with the requested five-sample centered mean; the remaining difference becomes residual.

steps.title: Inspect all three streams
steps.text: The final display matches the public xPatch-inspired operator at the stated configuration.

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.effect: Weights the newest observation in the EMA level update; the other weight is 1 - alpha.

parameters.name: ma_type
parameters.effect: Selects ema or the implemented Holt-style level/slope recurrence called dema.

parameters.name: season_smooth
parameters.effect: Optionally smooths the nontrend stream with an odd centered mean; omission leaves a zero derived residual.

parameters.name: beta
parameters.effect: Controls the slope update when ma_type='dema'; it does not affect the EMA path shown.

cautions: This operator does not run the complete xPatch forecasting architecture.
The source's dema option is a level/slope recurrence; interpret it from the code rather than assuming every library uses the same DEMA definition.
With season_smooth enabled, the seasonal stream uses centered smoothing even though EMA itself is one-sided.
When alpha is omitted, trend_window can derive it. Explicit alpha takes precedence.

references.title: Stitsyuk and Choi (2024), xPatch: Dual-Stream Time Series Forecasting with Exponential Seasonal-Trend Decomposition
